props.gloss_en: over bread one says 'hamotzi lechem min haaretz'
the Rabbanan hold that 'hamotzi' connotes 'brought out'
R' Nechemya's verse, as Rava gives it: '...who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt' (Ex 6:7)

that verse means: the Holy One said to Israel -- when I bring you out, I will do something for you so that you will know that it is I who brought you out of Egypt ('and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, hamotzi')
the Rabbanan praised the son of Rav Zevid to R' Zeira: he is a great man and expert in blessings
they brought him bread; he opened and said 'motzi'
R' Zeira: had he said 'hamotzi', he would have taught us the meaning, and taught us that the halakha follows the Rabbanan
and he did it to take himself out of the dispute
for we hold like the Rabbanan, who say it connotes 'brought out'

supports.gloss_en: דקיימא לן כרבנן דאמרי דאפיק משמע -- the wording is hamotzi because we hold like the Rabbanan

objections.gloss_en: ורבנן? -- and the Rabbanan: what of 'who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt' (Ex 6:7), which R' Nechemya reads as 'brings out'?

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא הכי קאמר -- God tells Israel: when I bring you out I will do something so you know it was I who brought you out; in 'and you shall know... hamotzi' the bringing-out is already past (= p_vidatem_afik)

objections.gloss_en: זה הוא שאומרים עליו דאדם גדול הוא ובקי בברכות הוא?! בשלמא אי אמר המוציא... אלא דאמר מוציא מאי קא משמע לן? -- is this the expert in blessings? 'hamotzi' would have taught the meaning and the halakha; 'motzi' teaches nothing

answered_by.gloss_en: ואיהו דעבד לאפוקי נפשיה מפלוגתא -- he said 'motzi' to take himself out of the dispute (= p_lafukei_mipluta)
